summary: Steel fire tower on Gilson Mountain in Fletcher, taken down in 1955 and moved to Bear Hill; no source here describes the Gilson site today.

facts.status_note: Taken down in 1955 and moved to Bear Hill, Allis State Park, Brookfield. Which structure stands there now is not confirmed.

events.note: Steel tower, 72 1/2 feet high, reported on Gilson Mountain; build date not in these sources
Lightning protection installed on tower and cabin (1942-44 report)
Telephone connected, stairs and landing painted, new cook stove (1949-50 report)
Steel tower taken down and moved to Bear Hill, Allis State Park, Brookfield

evidence.supports: tower in Fletcher, Franklin County; dismantling July 1955; to replace wooden tower on Bear Hill
evidence.quote: Last week a start was made on dismantling the Gilson Mountain tower in Fletcher, Franklin County. The steel tower will replace the wooden one on Bear Hill at Allis state park, Brookfield.

evidence.supports: 1936 steel tower 72 1/2 feet, highest in the state
evidence.quote: A steel tower, 72 1/2 feet high (the highest in the state) on Gilson Mountain.

evidence.supports: telephone line rebuilt after logging operator destroyed it
evidence.quote: The Gilson Mountain telephone line had to be rebuilt due to its destruction by a logging operator.

evidence.supports: lightning protection on tower and cabin
evidence.quote: Lightning protection was installed non the Gilson tower and cabin.

evidence.supports: cab painted and grounding system installed
evidence.quote: Painted tower cab outside and inside. Tower grounding system installed.

evidence.supports: 1949-50 new telephone, stairs and landing painted, new cook stove
evidence.quote: New telephone connected, tower stairs and landing painted and new cook stove installed.

evidence.supports: station discontinued; tower taken down and moved to Bear Hill; telephone salvaged
evidence.quote: This station was discontinued as a fire lookout. The steel tower was taken down and moved to Bear Hill and the telephone line was salvaged.

evidence.supports: former area now patrolled by an airplane observer
evidence.quote: The area formerly covered by this tower is now patrolled by an airplane observer.
Established in 1928, Allis State Park was the second state park to be created in Vermont.

evidence.quote: On Thursday, the state kicks off a project to maintain and improve fire towers.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The July 1955 Rutland Daily Herald item says the steel tower will replace the wooden one on Bear Hill; the 1955-56 biennial report says it was taken down and moved there. The story follows the biennial report.

sources.title: State lands fire tower restoration starting soon
Some Vermont fire towers to close for maintenance

notes_for_editor: The 1936 height is 72 1/2 feet; height_m is converted (22.1). Whether the Bear Hill tower today is the 1955 steel tower is unconfirmed. A geocaching listing (GC733D) says the current steel tower dates from 1966 and replaced a 1933 wooden one; we could not read its text beyond the title, so it is not cited. If it is right, the 1955 move did not produce the present tower. Ask Vermont FPR. Year 2025 for WCAX is taken from its URL. No source describes the Gilson site today.
